'''Sanjay Puri''' (born 23 November 1961) is an Indian statistical physicist and a senior professor at the School of Physical Sciences of [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]]. Known for his research on non-linear dynamics, Puri is an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Indian National Science Academy]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the [[Government of India]] for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to physical sciences in 2006.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx |title=View Bhatnagar Awardees |date=2017-11-11 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=2017-11-11}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link - please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:JNU Admin.JPG|thumb|left|Jawaharlal Nehru University]]
Born on 23 November 1961 at [[Rampur, Uttar Pradesh|Rampur]] in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]], Sanjay Puri earned a research-based master's degree (MS), guided by K. P. Jain, for his thesis, ''Theoretical Investigations of Soliton Dynamics'' in 1982 from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]].<ref name="Biographical Information - Sanjay Puri">{{Cite web |url=https://www.jnu.ac.in/Faculty/spuri/CV.pdf |title=Biographical Information - Sanjay Puri |date=2017-10-23 |website=Jawaharlal Nehru University |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref> Moving to the US, he secured another master's degree in physics from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 1983 and continued there for his doctoral studies under guidance of Yoshitsugu Oono to secure a PhD in 1987, his thesis being ''Some Problems in the Dynamics of Spatially Extended Systems.''.<ref name="Biography on PB Works">{{Cite web |url=http://mohitpuri.pbworks.com/w/page/61211655/Dr%20Sanjay%20Puri%20Eminent%20Professor%20in%20Jawaharlal%20Nehru%20University%20%20New%20Delhi |title=Biography on PB Works |date=2017-10-23 |website=PB Works |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref> Returning to India, Puri joined [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] the same year as an assistant professor at the School of Physical Sciences, became an associate professor in 1993 and has been working there as a professor since 2001. During this period, he also had several stints abroad as a visiting professor at institutions such as [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]], [[University of Manchester]], [[Cambridge University]] and [[Kyoto University]].<ref name="Profile on IIT Indore">{{Cite web |url=http://iiti.ac.in/Seminars/Abstract/Dr_Puri.pdf |title=Profile on IIT Indore |date=2017-10-23 |website=IIT Indore |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
[[File:Collision de solitons hydrodynamiques.png|thumb|150px|Collision of two [[solitons]].]]
The core areas of Puri's work are in [[statistical physics]] and [[nonlinear dynamics]]<ref name="Author profile">{{cite book|author1=Sanjay Puri|author2=Vinod Wadhawan|title=Kinetics of Phase Transitions - Author profile|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UX05bt7kI_IC&pg=PR9|date=24 March 2009|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4200-0836-4|pages=9–}}</ref> with special focus on [[pattern formation]] in [[Non-equilibrium thermodynamics|nonequilibrium systems]].<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P12-1584 |title=Indian fellow |date=2017-10-21 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-22}}</ref> His research is reported to have studied the effects of confined geometries and the role of defects in phase separation dynamics<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=244 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017-10-21 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=2017-10-21}}</ref> and the work is known to have assisted in a wider understanding of kinetics of phase ordering.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |date=2017-10-17 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref> Study of [[granular material]]s, especially freely-evolving [[Granular material#Granular gases|granular gases]], was another focal point of his work. Puri's studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/9065530_Sanjay_Puri |title=On ResearchGate |date=2017-10-17 |access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref><ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=mkcPLrEAAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2017-10-17 |publisher=Google Scholar |access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and the online article repository of the Indian Academy of Sciences has listed 134 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Puri=3ASanjay=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017-10-21 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=2017-10-21}}</ref> Besides, he has published three books,<ref name="Distinguished Alumni Award Citation">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iitd.ac.in/convocation/2013/DAA_SanjayPuri.pdf |title=Distinguished Alumni Award Citation |date=2017-10-23 |website=IIT Delhi |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref> including ''Dissipative Phenomena in Condensed Matter: Some Applications'', co-authored with [[Sushanta Kumar Dattagupta]]<ref name="DattaguptaPuri2013">{{cite book|author1=Sushanta Dattagupta|author2=Sanjay Puri|title=Dissipative Phenomena in Condensed Matter: Some Applications|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CbPrCAAAQBAJ|date=9 March 2013|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-662-06758-1}}</ref> and ''Kinetics of Phase Transitions'', an edited work.<ref name="PuriWadhawan2009">{{cite book|author1=Sanjay Puri|author2=Vinod Wadhawan|title=Kinetics of Phase Transitions|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UX05bt7kI_IC|date=24 March 2009|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4200-0836-4}}</ref> Puri has also guided several students in their studies<ref name="Awadesh Kumar Dubey">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cuh.ac.in/pdf/BTECH/awadesh.pdf |title=Awadesh Kumar Dubey |date=2017-10-23 |website=Central University of Haryana |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref><ref name="Prasenjit Das">{{Cite web |url=https://sites.google.com/site/prasenjithomepage/home |title=Prasenjit Das |date=2019-09-25 |website=Google Sites |access-date=2019-09-25}}</ref> and serves as the associate editor of ''Phase Transitions'' journal of [[Taylor & Francis|Taylor and Francis]].<ref name="Editorial board">{{Cite web |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=gpht20 |title=Editorial board |date=2017-10-23 |website=Taylor and Francis |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Puri, who topped the IIT Delhi examinations in 1982, was a recipient of the Silver Medal of Excellence of the institute.<ref name="Biographical Information - Sanjay Puri" /> The [[Indian National Science Academy]] awarded him the Young Scientist Medal in 1993<ref name="INSA Young Scientists Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/youngmedal.php |title=INSA Young Scientists Medal |date=2017-10-17 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-17 |archive-date=11 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511084357/https://www.insaindia.res.in/youngmedal.php }}</ref> and the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] selected him as an associate member in 1994.<ref name="Biography on PB Works" /> Puri received the N. S. Satya Murthy Memorial Award of the Indian Physics Association in 1994<ref name="Distinguished Alumni Award Citation" /> followed by B. M. Birla Science Prize in 1999.<ref name="B. M. Birla Science Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://www.birlasciencecentre.org/awards/birlaSciencePrizes/ |title=B. M. Birla Science Prize |date=2017-10-23 |website=B. M. Birla Science Centre |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref> He was chosen for the Homi Bhabha Fellowship in 2003<ref name="Homi Bhabha Fellowship">{{Cite web |url=http://homibhabhafellowships.com/HomiBhabhaFellow.aspx?id=69 |title=Homi Bhabha Fellowship |date=2017-10-23 |website=Homi Bhabha Council |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref> and for the J. C. Bose National Fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] in 2012.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> In between, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 2006.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> Puri is also an elected fellow of two of the three major Indian science academies, the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] electing him in 2006<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Puri,_Prof._Sanjay |title=Fellow profile |date=2017-10-21 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=2017-10-22}}</ref> and the Indian National Science Academy fellowship reaching him in 2012.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-23}}</ref>
